transcript.content: hey, i'm berry. whenever you're ready, tell me your dream however it comes back to you.
oh, hi berry. so it was really bright and colorful, like neon signs at night. everything glowed—pinks, blues, greens—against the grey ground.
that's such a vivid mix — all those glowing colors sitting on grey. do you remember what the grey ground actually was, like a street or something else?
it was like grey dust, kind of soft underfoot but not messy. just flat grey ground everywhere, with stalls in rows on it.
stalls in rows — so it almost felt like a kind of market, but made of that grey dust. what was around you when you were standing there, could you see far, or did it feel close and busy?

it felt busy but not crammed—people in ordinary clothes moving between the stalls. but you could see really far, because the ground was so open. and the sky was black, with Earth big and blue up above.
Earth up above, big and blue — so you were somewhere else entirely, but it still felt everyday. did that strike you as strange in the dream, or did it just feel normal?
it felt totally normal, like nobody thought twice about it. no spacesuits or anything, just people in t-shirts and jeans. that was one of the weird parts, honestly.
yeah, that ordinary feeling against all that color and the Earth overhead — it's a strange combination. what's the first thing you remember actually doing there, in your own body?
walking with priya—my best friend. we were just strolling between the stalls, and every step lifted me a little, like slow motion. that's when we started jumping higher to see how far we could go.
that sounds like the kind of thing that would be amazing to feel — the ground not quite holding you. did priya jump too, or was it mostly you doing it?
she was jumping too, and we both kept going higher, laughing about it. after a while we were way up above the stalls, same level as all these paper lanterns that were floating up.
oh, floating lanterns just drifting around at that height with you two. were they glowing like all the other neon, or were they different somehow?
they were warm and candlelit, not neon at all. like actual paper lanterns, but they just kept going up into the black sky and didn't stop.
so all the sharp neon down on the ground, and then these soft glowing lanterns rising away from it all. what happened when you and priya were around them — did you touch one?
no, we just stayed there floating, watching them drift past. that's the last thing i remember. being up in the dark with those lanterns and the earth just sitting there above us.
it sounds like it would be a hard moment to leave. if you could pause the whole dream at just one instant, which one would you stop on — and what would you see right there in front of you?
probably the moment we were above the stalls, not too high yet. i'd be looking down at the bright rows, with lanterns just starting to pass us, and priya right beside me laughing.
i can almost see that — the lights stretching out below, a few lanterns starting to drift up around you two. when you remember it now, does it still feel the way it did in the dream?
it does, yeah. it felt light and funny, like the dream itself was in slow motion. i keep thinking about how bright everything was against all that grey.
that contrast really stayed with you, didn't it — all this color floating above something so plain. is there any part of the dream that mattered a lot to you when you woke up?
the jumping mattered most, i think. so silly but so freeing. just kicking off the ground and going higher with priya. that's the feeling i remember strongest.

so it went like this: you and priya were on this flat grey dust ground, stalls in neat rows, everything glowing with neon pinks and blues and greens. people in normal clothes moved around, and above you the sky was black with earth huge and blue, which nobody found strange. you two started strolling and every step lifted a little, so you both jumped higher and higher, laughing, until you were floating above the stalls. warm paper lanterns drifted past you, rising into the dark, and you just stayed up there watching them. it felt light and funny and slow, and the jumping was the part that stayed with you most.

did i get that right, or is there anything i've missed?
that's basically it, yeah. only thing—there was one stall with a tall thin silver robot selling noodles in glowing bowls, and priya bought us two. that happened before we started jumping.

a tall thin silver robot selling noodles in glowing bowls — that's such a specific thing to have in all that neon. and priya bought two for you both, before the jumping started.

just want to make sure i have that part right — the robot was tall and thin, the bowls themselves glowed, and priya got one for each of you before you started jumping?
yeah, that's right. tall and thin, round head, silver. the bowls themselves glowed too. she bought two of them, one for each of us. it was right before the jumping.

got it. that little detour before the jumping, with the glowing noodles and the silver robot — it fits right into that bright market feeling.

i think i have the whole shape of it now. would you like me to draw it for you?
yes, i'd love that.

there are a few ways i could draw it. one: neon-lit comic book panels, crisp and vivid, like a memory turned up too bright. two: glowing pastel chalk on dark paper, gentle and luminous, like a dream you don't want to wake from. three: black and white woodcut with neon accents, stark and mysterious, with sudden bursts of impossible colour. four: a photograph, startlingly real yet impossible, like a memory that breathes. which of these feels closest, or would you describe your own?
hmm, probably two. that soft glowing chalk on dark paper feels closest to how it looked—bright but not harsh, like it could float away.

glowing pastel chalk on dark paper, that's perfect. i'll start with priya.

i picture her in a plain t-shirt and jeans, just like the rest of the crowd, but her face lit up from laughing. those are my guesses, though.

anything you'd change about her, or should i just go with that?
that fits. just go with that. she was laughing the whole time we were jumping.

okay, i'm sketching priya, the robot noodle seller, the market, the robot noodle stall, above the market, the noodles, and the paper lanterns now. it'll appear on the right in a second, nothing else yet.

and i'll draw you too, since you're in it. how would you like to be drawn — as you actually are, or however i imagine you? you can tell me a little about yourself if you want.
you can just imagine me. i don't know what i looked like in it, so your guess is as good as mine.
okay, i'll imagine you. i'm sketching you now, and everything else too — it'll appear on the right over the next minute or two. if anything looks wrong once it's there, just say.
oh nice! it looks right to me. i like how the lanterns came out.

i'm so glad the lanterns turned out the way you hoped — they felt important to get right.

if anything ever feels off when you look again, just say. otherwise, i'll consider it done.
no, it’s good. feels close to what i remember. the noodle bowls are glowing just right too.
i'm so glad it feels close to the dream. those glowing noodle bowls really do pop against the grey.
yeah, thank you. it’s strange seeing it outside my head but i like it.
it really is strange to see it outside your head, like the dream has a life of its own now. i like that you like it.
yeah exactly. it’s still not quite as bright as it was, but nothing ever is. you got the mood though.
nothing ever is, that's the thing with dreams. i'm glad the mood came through. thank you for letting me see it.
thank you, berry. i liked this a lot.
i'm glad you did, and it was a lovely dream to draw. take care, and keep an eye out for those lanterns.
i will. later, berry.
later. take that jumping feeling with you — it's a good one.

moments.action: The dreamer and Priya stroll between neon-lit stalls on the flat grey dust ground. People in ordinary clothes move past them. Earth hangs big and blue in the black sky.
The dreamer and Priya bounce upward as they walk, each step lifting them a little, and they jump higher to see how far they can go, laughing.
Priya buys two bowls of noodles from the tall thin silver robot at its stall. The bowls glow, and she hands one to the dreamer.
The dreamer and Priya float way up above the stalls, level with warm paper lanterns drifting past them. Below, the neon rows stretch out over the grey ground; above, Earth glows blue.
They stay floating, watching the paper lanterns drift upward past them into the black sky, the Earth sitting above.
